Question: Let \(o\) be an odd whole number and let \(n\) be any whole number. Which of the following statements about the whole number \(o^2 + no\) is always true?

Choices.C: it is even only if \(n\) is even
Choices.D: it is odd only if \(n\) is odd
Choices.E: it is odd only if \(n\) is even

Solution:
Because \(o\) is odd, \(o^2=o\times o\) is odd. Multiplying by the odd number \(o\) also preserves whether \(n\) is even or odd. There are two cases:

If \(n\) is even, including \(0\), then \(no\) is even. Thus \(o^2+no\) is odd plus even, which is odd.

If \(n\) is odd, then \(no\) is odd. Thus \(o^2+no\) is odd plus odd, which is even.

Every whole number \(n\) belongs to exactly one of these cases. Therefore the expression is odd exactly when \(n\) is even. In particular, it is odd only if \(n\) is even, choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
